name: Björk
label: One Little Independent
lede: She cut an LP at eleven, opened for Crass at seventeen, started Iceland's biggest rock band at twenty, and has spent every album since refusing to make the last one again.

eras.title: A punk kid in a small city
eras.text: An LP at eleven, then teenage bands in a city small enough that everyone shared a rehearsal room. The voice gets loud in Tappi Tíkarrass and louder in Kukl.

years.h: At eleven, a school recital on national radio gets Björk a record deal
years.p: Teachers sent a recording of her singing Tina Charles's "I Love to Love" to the RÚV radio station, which broadcast it nationally. The label Fálkinn offered a contract, and her self-titled album came out in Iceland in December 1977.
years.xp: Björk Guðmundsdóttir was born in Reykjavík on 21 November 1965 and had been studying classical piano and flute since about age six, according to Wikipedia. The recital recording is how the label found her.

years.h: Tappi Tíkarrass takes its name from a bassist's father
years.p: "Cork the Bitch's Ass": Jakob Smári Magnússon's father said their music fitted like one. Björk replaces original singer [[Eyþór Arnalds|d405bc70-32de-4cab-8efe-efbddc9551a4]] within months.
years.xp: The band came out of the wreckage of Jam-80 in September 1981. Arnalds went on to study cello and later became mayor of Árborg.

yt: Tappi Tíkarrass live in Reykjavík, 28 August 1982
years.h: Bitið fast í vitið is Tappi Tíkarrass's first record
years.p: Spor puts out the EP in August 1982 with Björk singing lead, a year before she leaves for Kukl.

yt: Tappi Tíkarrass, "Hrollur", from Rokk í Reykjavík
years.h: The teenage Björk lands on the VHS cover of Rokk í Reykjavík
years.p: Tappi Tíkarrass contribute two songs to the 1982 documentary of Iceland's punk scene, and Björk is the face on the tape.

years.h: Kukl open for Crass in Reykjavík, and Crass offer them a deal
years.p: Björk leaves Tappi Tíkarrass for Kukl, assembled in August 1983 by Ásmundur Jónsson of Gramm Records. The first show is on 20 September.
years.xp:
The six-piece was Björk, trumpeter and vocalist [[Einar Örn Benediktsson|4c99c75d-e9a0-46c7-bb1f-7a9f65417914]], keyboardist Einar Arnaldur Melax, bassist Birgir Mogensen, drummer [[Sigtryggur Baldursson|c7d8ab0c-292f-4651-9edf-2d79de385382]] and guitarist Guðlaugur Kristinn Óttarsson.

Crass headlined the festival show, and their label, Crass Records, offered Kukl a deal afterward.

years.h: The Eye comes out on Crass Records, produced by Penny Rimbaud
years.p: Kukl's first album is made with Rimbaud of Crass. They tour Europe in 1985 and become the first Icelandic band at Roskilde.
years.xp: The 1985 tour also took in the Pandora's Box Festival in the Netherlands.

eras.title: Bad Taste goes pop
eras.text: Kukl's survivors build an art collective into a label, a book press and a pop band. Then one single about a birthday carries them out of Reykjavík.

years.h: The Sugarcubes form around an art collective called Bad Taste
years.p: [[Einar Örn Benediktsson|4c99c75d-e9a0-46c7-bb1f-7a9f65417914]] and [[Þór Eldon|1e4afef3-c22e-4776-8773-db4d13fa28ca]] had started Smekkleysa as an art collective that grew into a label and a book publisher. The band forms on top of it on 8 June 1986.
years.xp:
The line-up was Björk (vocals, keyboards), Einar Örn (vocals, trumpet), Eldon (guitar), Bragi Ólafsson (bass) and Sigtryggur Baldursson (drums). Björk and Eldon's son, Sindri Eldon, was born the same day.

The first single, a double A-side of "Ammæli" and "Köttur", came out in Iceland on 21 November 1986, Björk's 21st birthday.

years.h: Holidays in Europe is Kukl's last record
years.p: Björk, Einar Örn, Melax and Sigtryggur carry on as the Sugarcubes. Björk and guitarist Guðlaugur Óttarsson briefly record as the Elgar Sisters.

years.src: Wikipedia: Birthday (The Sugarcubes song) · Wikipedia: The Sugarcubes
years.h: Melody Maker and NME both make Birthday single of the week
years.p: The English version, out on One Little Indian, reaches John Peel, and listeners vote it No. 1 in his 1987 Festive Fifty.
years.xp:
It was the band's first UK chart entry, at No. 65, and went to No. 1 on the UK independent chart. The Icelandic original, "Ammæli", had been on the Iceland-only single "Einn Mol'á Mann" and became a B-side abroad.

Jim and William Reid of the Jesus and Mary Chain remixed it in 1988 as "Birthday (The Christmas Mixes)".

years.src: Wikipedia: Birthday (The Sugarcubes song) · Wikipedia: The Sugarcubes · Wikipedia: Björk
years.h: Life's Too Good is the first Icelandic album to land worldwide
years.p: It sells past a million copies, and the band plays Saturday Night Live on 15 October 1988.
years.xp: Matthew Broderick hosted that SNL, and the band played "Birthday" and "Motorcrash". The "Birthday" single came 15th in the 1988 Village Voice Pazz & Jop critics' poll.

years.h: Gling-Gló is a jazz album sung in Icelandic
years.p: Björk makes it with Tríó Guðmundar Ingólfssonar during a Sugarcubes break, mixing standards with originals.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls it her best-selling album in Iceland as of 2011. The same year she sang on 808 State's ex:el and met the harpist Corky Hale, whose session later landed on Debut.

years.h: Stick Around for Joy is the Sugarcubes' last album
years.p: Wikipedia calls it a contractual obligation, though it did better with critics than the record before it and produced the single "Hit".
years.xp: The band's final show was in Reykjavík. Wikipedia lists the breakup as December 1992, and the only reunion was a one-off Reykjavík concert on 17 November 2006, with profits going to Smekkleysa.

years.big: "The biggest rock band to emerge from Iceland"
years.h: The Sugarcubes end with a final show in Reykjavík
years.p: Rolling Stone's epitaph, as Wikipedia quotes it. Björk was already recording in London.

eras.title: A house in London, a new producer
eras.text: With Nellee Hooper and a pile of collaborators, Björk stops being the Sugarcubes' singer and becomes a solo act with her own pop hits.

years.h: Debut sells 600,000 copies in three months, not 40,000
years.p: One Little Indian had guessed 40,000 copies worldwide. Nellee Hooper produced most of it, and Björk alone made "The Anchor Song".
years.xp:
It reached No. 3 in the UK and No. 61 in the US, went platinum there and has sold 4.7 million copies worldwide, per Wikipedia.

At the 1994 Brit Awards she won Best Newcomer and Best International Female. Michel Gondry's "Human Behaviour" video, which Björk picked after seeing his work with the band Oui Oui, was nominated for a Grammy and lost to Peter Gabriel's "Steam".

years.h: Post brings in Tricky, Howie B and Graham Massey
years.p: [[Nellee Hooper|320dc49d-621b-4e46-8273-2e9d34bbfa01]] produces again, and Spin later ranks the album No. 7 of the 1990s.
years.xp: It came out in June 1995 and went platinum in the US, with several UK hit singles.

years.h: A stalker sends the next album from London to Málaga
years.p: Homogenic was planned for her London home. After a stalker incident involving Ricardo López and the media disruption around it, she records in a Málaga studio offered by her tour drummer Trevor Morais.
years.xp: Wikipedia is the source for the relocation. I left out further details of the incident.

eras.title: Málaga, Cannes, then whispers
eras.text: A Spanish studio, a film set and a world of microbeats, one record each. Her widest fame, and her quietest music.

yt: "All Is Full of Love" (dir. Chris Cunningham)
years.h: Homogenic puts an Icelandic string octet over Mark Bell's beats
years.p: Mark Bell, Howie B, Guy Sigsworth and Markus Dravs produce with Björk, and Eumir Deodato writes the string parts she didn't arrange herself.
years.xp:
Wu-Tang Clan nearly contributed but were tied up with their own album. It reached No. 4 in the UK and No. 28 in the US, and Rolling Stone later put it at No. 202 on its 500 Greatest Albums list.

Of Bell, Björk said: "If I were to say who has influenced me most it would be Stockhausen, Kraftwerk, Brian Eno and Mark Bell."

The clip is the 1999 video for "All Is Full of Love", directed by Chris Cunningham.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dancer in the Dark · Wikipedia: Björk
years.h: Björk, who never wanted to act, wins Best Actress at Cannes
years.p: Lars von Trier asked her to score Dancer in the Dark, then talked her into the lead. The film took the Palme d'Or.
years.xp:
She played Selma Ježková, a factory worker going blind who steals to pay for her son's sight-saving operation. She said afterward she wasn't put off acting by the film, only that she had never wanted to act at all and made an exception for von Trier.

"I've Seen It All", co-written with Sjón and von Trier, was nominated for the Oscar for Best Original Song and lost to Bob Dylan's "Things Have Changed". She performed it at the 2001 ceremony in the swan dress.

yt: Live at the Royal Opera House, London, 2001
years.h: Vespertine trades stadium volume for harps and microbeats
years.p: Matmos, harpist Zeena Parkins and Thomas Knak supply the small sounds, and the tour plays theaters and opera houses.
years.xp:
It started as a concept called "Domestika", about everyday domestic life. Critic Mark Pytlik wrote that she "had set out to write an album about making sandwiches...She'd ended up with an album about making love."

It debuted at No. 19 on the Billboard 200 with 75,000 copies in its first week, and Metacritic has it at 88 from 28 reviews. The tour added an Inuit women's choir and conductor Simon Lee.

eras.title: All voices, then a map
eras.text: A record made almost entirely of voices, a dress that opens into a map of the world, and her first US top ten. One last Sugarcubes night in between.

years.cap: Björk at the Hurricane Festival, Germany
years.h: Medúlla is built almost entirely from human voices
years.p: Tanya Tagaq, Rahzel, Mike Patton and Robert Wyatt sing alongside choirs, and it debuts at No. 14 on the US chart.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the record uses voices plus basic electronic programming and occasional instruments. One track sets E.E. Cummings.

years.h: A dress unfurls into a world map as Björk sings at the Athens Olympics
years.p: She sang "Oceania" at the opening ceremony in August 2004. The 10,000 square foot map flowed out over the athletes.
years.xp: The song was written for the occasion, with beatboxer Shlomo and a London choir. A version with Kelis circulated online and ended up as a B-side to "Who Is It".

years.h: The Sugarcubes get back together for one night at Laugardalshöll
years.p: A 20th-anniversary concert on 17 November 2006, with profits going to Smekkleysa. They said they had no plans for more shows or new material.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band confirmed it had no plans for further shows or recording.

years.cap: Björk's Volta-tour stage with the Reactable, Coachella, April 2007
years.h: Volta debuts at No. 9, her first US top ten
years.p: Timbaland and Antony are on the record, and the tour carries a brass band and the Reactable, a touch-table instrument. First-week sales: 43,000.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia it sold 43,000 copies in its first US week. Guests included Toumani Diabaté, Konono No. 1 and [[Antony Hegarty|91b67275-db2c-4fc2-b51f-82978aeb5c41]]; the tour ran about 18 months and returned to Latin America after nine years.

eras.title: Apps, then a breakup record
eras.text: An iPad app per song and a museum retrospective, then the most personal record she has made. It leaked two months early.

years.h: Biophilia ships as an iPad app, one per song
years.p: First shown at the Manchester International Festival on 30 June 2011, with a gameleste built for the record.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls it the first album released as a series of interactive apps. It came with custom instruments and educational programs for Reykjavík schoolchildren.

years.h: Vulnicura leaks two months early, so Björk releases it on the 20th
years.p: A breakup record made with [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]] and the Haxan Cloak, about the end of her relationship with Matthew Barney. She put it on iTunes on 20 January rather than wait for March.
years.xp:
The leak was 18 January. The physical release followed on 16 March. The title means "cure for wounds" in Latin.

She approached Arca after getting a mixtape from him, and they began working after he DJed an afterparty on the Biophilia tour. Metacritic has the album at 87 from 40 reviews.

years.h: MoMA opens a Björk retrospective with a room of 49 hidden speakers
years.p: It ran 8 March to 7 June 2015, pairing instruments built for Biophilia with a video installation for "Black Lake".
years.xp: Videos for "Lionsong" and "Black Lake" premiered at the museum that March.

years.h: Arca returns for Utopia, which Wikipedia calls a "Tinder album"
years.p: Her second record with Arca goes looking for love and for a utopia.
years.xp: It was nominated for a Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album. The 2019 staged show Cornucopia opened at The Shed in New York's Hudson Yards.

eras.title: Underground
eras.text: After her mother died in 2018 she made a record about what lives under the ground, then kept collaborating at the edges.

years.h: Björk's daughter makes her film debut in The Northman
years.p: Robert Eggers's film, co-written by Sjón, reached US cinemas on 22 April 2022. Björk appears in it.

years.cap: Björk performing Björk Orkestral at Bluedot Festival, UK, July 2022
years.src: Wikipedia: Fossora · Album of the Year: Fossora · Metacritic: Fossora
years.h: Björk plans a clarinet album, then adds gabber halfway through
years.p: Fossora, her tenth album and first as sole producer, mourns her mother Hildur Rúna Hauksdóttir, who died in 2018. Pitchfork gave it 8.4; Metacritic has 85 from 22 reviews.
years.xp:
She told Pitchfork: "This is the clarinet album! Then halfway through, I was like, 'Fuck that.'" Guests include Serpentwithfeet, her children Sindri and Ísadóra, the clarinet sextet Murmuri and the Indonesian dance duo Gabber Modus Operandi. Arca couldn't join because of pandemic travel restrictions.

"Sorrowful Soil" is a eulogy for Hildur Rúna and "Ancestress" an epitaph. It reached No. 11 in the UK and No. 100 in the US, and Pitchfork ranked it No. 12 of 2022.

years.cap: Björk on the Cornucopia tour, Paris, September 2023
years.h: Rosalía joins Björk on "Oral" to defend a fjord
years.p: Sega Bodega produced the single, and proceeds went to Aegis, which Björk co-founded with other Icelandic activists to oppose Norwegian fish farming in Seyðisfjörður.
years.xp: Rosalía returned the favor on "Berghain" in 2025, per Wikipedia.
